gap_eur.long_label: Target spend for the market minus what we billed for parts

color_scale.note: Continuous ramp on a square-root scale. Euro values span two orders of magnitude across these markets, so equal-width colour bands would put every market except three in the palest class.

capture_vs_max.label: Share of target spend captured
capture_vs_max.long_label: Parts billed divided by the target spend for the market

color_scale.note: Class breaks sit in the gaps between natural clusters in the 2025 data, not on round numbers: 35% | 40-55% (six markets) | 55-70% (four) | 70-85% (four) | 84-92% (three).

spend_per_unit_eur.label: What we billed per truck
spend_per_unit_eur.long_label: Parts billed divided by the vehicles in service

color_scale.note: Observed range EUR 88 to 389 across the 18 markets.

total_sales_eur.label: Parts billed
total_sales_eur.long_label: Parts revenue billed into the market

max_spend_eur.label: Target spend for the market
max_spend_eur.long_label: Modelled parts spend the market should support

height.note: Column height above ground, read by MapLibre as fill-extrusion height in metres. The gap ranges from EUR 16,218 to EUR 6,271,367, a 387-fold spread, so every column gets a 35 km base from which the square root of the value adds up to 700 km. On a plain linear scale the smallest fifteen markets would be a flat line, and the floor is what makes a small gap still clickable and visible.

projection.note: Globe is the default. If the browser cannot paint the extruded columns on the globe, the toolbar switch drops to a flat map.

glossary.GPS: Global Parts Support — the parts-spend model that sets a target spend per truck.
glossary.PMS: Parts Market Scan — the model that compares what a market should buy against what it did buy.
glossary.UIO: Units In Operation — the vehicles in service that could buy parts.
